decision: Every command except history reconciles the files with the recorded projection before it runs, recording set/remove events for leaves that differ
reason: Hand edits made while nothing was running must become events (the new spec requires this)

decision: history never reconciles; once a state file exists it reads the recorded events without loading the files
reason: History reports what has been recorded; it needs no loadable files once something has been recorded

decision: history still loads the files and runs the first import when no state file exists yet
reason: It only loads them to perform the first import

decision: Every load-reconcile-write holds an exclusive flock on the .troupe directory itself rather than on a separate lock file
reason: set writes its files and records its events under the lock, so watch only sees the write-back after the events exist and emits nothing. Locking the directory needs no extra file in .troupe/

decision: watch polls file contents every 0.1 s instead of using OS file-change notifications
reason: No new dependency; covers includes outside .troupe/ or not yet existing; a change cannot fall between loading and watching

decision: watch compares the current bytes against exactly what was last loaded, including the config file, every include (text includes too) and the absent alternative config name (troupe.yml/troupe.yaml)
reason: So a change cannot fall between loading and starting to watch

decision: If watch cannot load the config at start, it exits 4 and does not print the watching line
If a later edit breaks the config, watch prints the error to stderr once (deduplicated by message) and keeps retrying until the files load again
reason: Mid-save edits or includes whose target is not written yet

decision: Reconcile emits sets in document order, then removes
reason: The same order as set's own events

decision: watch reconciles first, then prints 'watching <dir>' using the path exactly as passed (or as taken from TROUPE_THEATRE / '.')
watch exits 0 on SIGINT or SIGTERM, using a threading.Event set by signal handlers and restoring the previous handlers afterwards
The value comparison is type-sensitive (1 -> '1' counts as a change); formatting and comment edits produce no events
The leaf-diff logic is extracted from cli._set into a shared store.diff function that both set and reconcile use
Add ConfigStore.exists() and ConfigStore.reconcile(); _reconcile falls back to ensure_imported when there is no aggregate
Load the config before opening/creating the store so a failed load does not create the state DB (this replaced the first _sync design)
reason: The state DB must not be created when loading fails

decision: find_config is resolved before taking the lock, so the lock targets the directory that holds the config
Replace test_import_is_not_reconciling with test_import_happens_once
reason: The old test checked the opposite of what the new spec requires

decision: Update decision 2 in decisions.md: show still reads the files but now reconciles first, so the two agree
Test watch as a real subprocess with timing-based waits (2 s history timeout, 0.3-0.6 s sleeps), and rerun the sync tests 5 times to check for flakiness
reason: To check that the timing-dependent watch tests aren't flaky

decision: Test that set does not cause double events while watch runs, with set both in-process and in separate processes
Commit directly on main; skip the merge/PR/keep menu and do not push
reason: Nothing to merge since it was committed to main; pushing or opening a PR would break the delivery rule; no branch or worktree to clean up

decision: The parser now reads args.path with getattr, since the watch subcommand has no path argument
